decision: a trunk on a machine's port is refused, with the reason and vlan as the fix; no router on a stick
why: the guest kernel has no 802.1Q: ip link add link eth0 name eth0.10 type vlan id 10 answers RTNETLINK Not supported, and there is no /proc/net/vlan and no /lib/modules

decision: verbs vlan <port> <id> (port_vlan) and trunk <port> [--allow ids|all] [--native id] (port_trunk); the port is lan:3 or the NIC in it; defaults allow all, native 1
why: one verb and one tool per setting, beside plug, cable and link; a port is named as link names it
evidence: src/commands/verbs/vlan.ts; refusals.test.ts runs every verb's example from the bar and its tool

decision: a port's VLAN is the port's; a free port is access VLAN 1, kept in one place (settleVlans after every update), so unplug, a move, uncable, rm, a failure and rmswitch reset it; a cut, power off or reboot keep it; vlan on a free port is refused
why: a new holder never inherits a stale VLAN, and no command path has to remember the reset
evidence: src/model/vlans.test.ts: is 1 again once nothing is in the port

decision: the native VLAN is carried only when it is allowed; an access port carries a tagged frame as payload of its VLAN, as a switch that knows no VLANs would
why: Cisco semantics; box 4.2.4 says a VLAN the trunk does not allow does not cross it; the default port stays as it was for any frame

decision: capture entries keep the frame untagged, with the VLAN that carried it and a mask of the ports it had a tag on; a cable's .pcap puts the tag back as it was on that cable; vlan <id> matches the carried VLAN, not only tagged frames
why: decode, filters and ARP tracking stay as they were; a person asks which VLAN a frame was in, which a tag alone does not say on an access port

decision: saved labs are version 9 with vlans; version 8 opens with every port in VLAN 1
why: story 8.1

decision: an access port reads a frame's tag as a trunk does: it takes a frame tagged with its own VLAN or with VLAN 0, without the tag, and drops and counts one tagged with any other; this replaces 'an access port carries a tagged frame as payload' of 05:53
why: the payload rule let a trunk cabled to an access port tag a frame again on every lap, without end; most switches take a tagged frame on an access port only for the port's own VLAN (802.1Q ingress filtering); a tag that a trunk puts on now comes off at the next port or the frame is dropped there, so no wiring makes a frame longer; a default port now drops a frame that a guest tags with another VLAN, which no guest kernel here sends on its own; a frame with two tags, the port's own and then another, still hops to the other VLAN over a trunk whose native VLAN is the port's, as on real switches, and one tag alone no longer does
evidence: .audit/phase2/vlans/tagged-loop.mjs: 219,714 bytes, a RangeError and a dead cable in 82 s at cfd20a2; src/runtime/fabric.test.ts VLANs: an access port takes a frame tagged with its own VLAN; a cable from a trunk to an access port; test/integration/vlans.test.ts: a broadcast that loops from a trunk into an access port; a probe of both tag stacks on the fabric at cfd20a2 and after

decision: a port drops a frame longer than 1,514 bytes, or 1,518 with a tag, and counts it in the port's dropped; two tags get no more room than one
why: Ethernet's 1,500 bytes after the header, without the checksum that a guest's NIC does not hand over; the longest frame a guest sends in a TCP transfer is 1,514 bytes; a real switch with no jumbo setting drops a longer one; a wiring fault or a guest can then never make the lab carry or keep a frame of any size; story 5's MTU of a cable can only be lower
evidence: test/integration/nics.test.ts: the longest frame of a routed transfer is 1,514 bytes; src/runtime/fabric.test.ts VLANs: a port takes a frame of up to 1,514 bytes, or 1,518 with its tag

decision: the copies of a frame that a switch flooded share where they have come in: the first to come into a switch in a VLAN goes on at once, and what a switch sends on of a later copy waits its turn at the looped pace, under the same limit of 64 a cable, with no looped mark; the mark is as it was
why: since 39ea5fa a frame went at once until it came back to a switch in a VLAN it was in there, so one broadcast took every way through the switches and VLANs before anything paced it; four rules were measured on the same scripts; pacing a flood from a frame's second visit to any switch equals 4f9aa89 in a mesh, but holds broadcasts over a cable that joins two VLANs to the pace and drops 936 of 1,000 sent at once; a limit of cables crossed either slows a chain of switches or leaves 13,104 frames at once; sharing where copies came in leaves 51, costs a lab with one way to each switch nothing, and misses no loop in 54,000 random wirings
evidence: .audit/phase2/vlans/results/candidates.txt and fanout.txt: in a mesh of six with one join 1,370 frames at once at 4f9aa89, 32,471 at cfd20a2, 51 now; in 300 dense labs at most 1,341, 184,514 and 180, and the slowest broadcast 1 ms, 271 ms and under 1 ms; src/runtime/fabric.test.ts: one broadcast into a mesh of six switches; frames that go by the table cross a cable from one VLAN to another at once

decision: left as it is: a frame that a far switch turns round, so that it comes back to a switch in its first VLAN by the cable it left on, is marked as looped once, and the switch says it storms for a tenth of a second, though the frame ends there
why: it takes a trunk whose ends have different native VLANs and a cable that joins those two VLANs on the far switch; marking only a frame that comes back by the port it came in by before (c3b) removes every such mark and misses no loop, but then no loop is marked on its first way round, which four unit tests and the README describe; the second verifier rated it low
evidence: .audit/phase2/vlans/results/fuzz.txt: 4 of 3,000 wirings, 33 of 40,000, 14 of 10,000 dense ones; results/candidates.txt: c3b has 0 of 3,000 and 0 of 1,000; .audit/phase2/vlans/turned-round.mjs: a wiring of two switches that shows it

decision: every looped frame is given one shared record of what the next switch needs, and a copy on a cable has those fields written out, not spread
why: 0d91ca9 made a record for each frame a switch sent on and spread it into each copy; in a mesh storm that took the fabric 88 ms where cfd20a2 took 62, with longer garbage collections, and on the page the worst main-thread gap of a 20 s mesh storm rose from 6.7 ms to 7.7 ms; a looped frame needs no record of its own, as it had none before; each half was measured alone, and both were needed
evidence: .audit/phase2/vlans/results/storm-cost.txt: 62 ms at cfd20a2, 88 ms at 0b603f2, 66 ms after, medians of five; results/storm-mesh-1.txt: the worst gap on the page, 18 runs of cfd20a2 and of 0b603f2's source and 12 of this, p99 the same in all

decision: a cable's conditions are a field of the cable: of a NIC's plug and of a cable between switches, beside its cut. They go where the cable is moved, stay through a cut, a power off and a reboot, and are gone with the cable: unplug, uncable, rm, a failure, rmswitch. One rule in update()'s settle step tells the switches, by the port each cable is in
why: a list of conditions keyed by port, as VLANs have, would need a rule that moves an entry with its cable and one that drops it without, and conditions could outlive their cable; a cable is one thing a person makes bad, and its cut already works this way

decision: the fabric keeps a cable's conditions at the port it is in, as it keeps what a port carries, and a frame meets them once: where it leaves a switch, and from a machine before it comes into one. A NIC's cable with conditions is a queue in each direction, like a cable between switches, and is the direct call again once it has none and nothing waits in it
why: one design for both kinds of cable; a NIC's cable with no conditions keeps the direct call that the frames spike decided, so a lab with none runs the code it ran; the port keeps the setting through detach and attach, so the model tells the fabric only when a cable's conditions change
evidence: src/runtime/fabric.test.ts: conditions on a NIC's cable and on a cable between switches run the same tests; a NIC's cable

decision: the command is link <up|down> <cables> [--delay 100ms] [--loss 20%] [--reorder 25%] [--rate 1mbit] [--mtu 1400] [--clear], tool link_set. An option left out leaves that part, 0 takes one away (1500 for the MTU), --clear takes all away first. No new verb or tool
why: link already names every cable: a machine, a NIC, a port, a cable between switches by either port; story 1.1 allows an option; one tool fewer for an agent to choose between. Against it: a line that only sets conditions still says up or down, and link's description had to give up two sentences to stay within the 500 characters a tool has. A verb of its own (impair, or conditions) would have neither cost and one more tool
evidence: src/commands/verbs/link.test.ts link, with conditions; src/agent/agent.test.ts: within the lengths Chrome recommends
result: decided, for the user to confirm

decision: reordering is a share of frames that skip the delay, as in netem and as the frames spike measured, so --reorder without a delay is refused, and so is taking the delay away from a cable that reorders
why: a share that is held back instead would need a time of its own to explain; a setting that does nothing would be worse than a refusal that says what to add
evidence: src/model/conditions.test.ts: have reordering only with a delay; test/integration/link-conditions.test.ts

decision: a rate sends one frame at a time and holds 64 KiB that wait, in bytes, as the frames spike had it. A frame that would wait behind more is dropped with the reason rate
why: a bound in bytes is one comparison for each frame and holds 43 full frames, which TCP fills in slow start and then keeps busy: 0.952 Mbit/s of payload at 1 Mbit/s, which is 95.6% less the retransmissions

decision: a cable's MTU is of the packet that a frame holds: 14 bytes of header are not counted, and neither are the 4 of an 802.1Q tag. From 68 to 1500, where 1500 is none
why: that is what MTU means on a Linux interface, and what the fabric's own limit of 1,514 or 1,518 bytes already says; a trunk then carries the same packets as the access ports beside it
evidence: src/runtime/fabric.test.ts: a tag is not counted in a cable's MTU

decision: a frame that a cable dropped stays a frame of the capture, with the cable's port and the reason on it, and has no entry kind of its own. One that a machine's cable dropped before the switch had it is a frame from that port that went to none, and is not counted as taken in
why: the filter, the frame detail, the .pcap and capture_read then have dropped frames with no change, and a frame that the switch sent has one row and not two; the VLAN notes had proposed an entry kind
evidence: src/capture/cables.test.ts: the rows of frames that a cable dropped; e2e/link-conditions.spec.ts

decision: a cable with conditions holds at most 8,192 frames in each direction (HELD_LIMIT), where one with none holds 256. What does not fit is counted in the port's dropped frames, as a full cable's are, and is not in the capture with a reason
why: frames that wait for a delay are not a backlog: 256 would hold a 100 ms cable to 30 Mbit/s; 8,192 full frames are 12 MB at most in a direction, more than TCP's largest window puts on a cable; the frames spike had 65,536
evidence: src/runtime/fabric.test.ts: holds no more frames than its bound
result: decided; a UDP flood over a long delay is dropped with no row

decision: a change to a cable's conditions lets what was on its way arrive at once, in order
why: the spike left open whether to drop what waits or keep its order; due times order the queue, so frames sent after a change would overtake those sent before it; dropping them would lose pings on a cable that was just made good
evidence: src/runtime/fabric.test.ts: that change let what was on its way arrive at once

decision: each direction of a cable draws from two streams of its own, one for loss and one for reordering, once a frame. Math.random in the app, seeded (mulberry32, seed 20261126, written down before any result) in unit and integration tests
why: which frames are lost then depends only on their place in a direction, so the 1,000-frame checks give the same count each run; an unseeded cable fails within three points over 1,000 in 1.58% of runs (spike)

decision: counts are the switches' and never in the lab's state: commands read them through deps.carried, as the page reads port counters. They start again when a cable is plugged in and at a reload
why: story 8.1 has counters start empty; a count in the state would be an event a second for every cable with traffic

decision: saved labs are version 10: each NIC and each cable between switches has conditions. Version 9 opens with none
why: story 8.1
